                                  11                     Defendant.

Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           Pending before the Court is Plaintiff Sergey Firsov’s Motion to Disqualify Judge for

                                  14   Cause. ECF No. 14. Plaintiff argues: “Judge violated Amendments 5th and 14th to Constitution

                                  15   because destruction behavior and improper order to show cause without a fair hearing could raise

                                  16   due process concerns. Who will trust the judge who ignoring and not reading documents?” Mot.

                                  17   at 2. Plaintiff argues the undersigned “should recuse himself and move to different court.” Id.

                                  18           Motions to disqualify or recuse a judge fall under two statutory provisions, 28 U.S.C. §

                                  19   144 and 28 U.S.C. § 455. Section 144 requires a party seeking recusal to file a timely and

                                  20   sufficient affidavit averring that the judge before whom the matter is pending has a personal bias

                                  21   or prejudice either against the party or in favor of an adverse party, and setting forth the facts and

                                  22   reasons for such belief. 28 U.S.C. § 144. Similarly, § 455 requires a judge to disqualify himself

                                  23   “in any proceeding in which his impartiality might reasonably be questioned,” 28 U.S.C. § 455(a),

                                  24   including where the judge “has a personal bias or prejudice concerning a party, or personal

                                  25   knowledge of disputed evidentiary facts concerning the proceeding,” id. § 455 (b)(1). Section 455

                                  26   includes additional circumstances in which a judge must disqualify himself, none of which are

                                  27   relevant to the bases Plaintiff lists. See id. § 455 (b)(2)-(5).

                                  28           Here, Plaintiff has failed to establish any basis on which the Court’s impartiality might
                                         Case 3:25-cv-03387-TSH            Document 15         Filed 05/19/25      Page 2 of 2




                                   1   reasonably be questioned. The only evidence in support of his motion that Plaintiff provides is

                                   2   that the undersigned denied his application to proceed in forma pauperis and, after Plaintiff failed

                                   3   to pay the filing fee, ordered him to show cause why this case should not be dismissed. Mot. at 1.

                                   4   “Ordinarily, the alleged bias must stem from an ‘extrajudicial source.’” United States v.

                                   5   Hernandez, 109 F.3d 1450, 1454 (9th Cir. 1997) (citing Liteky v. United States, 510 U.S. 540,

                                   6   554-56 (1994)). Thus, while judicial rulings may constitute grounds for an eventual appeal, they

                                   7   are not a valid basis for a motion for recusal. See Liteky v. United States, 510 U.S. 540, 555

                                   8   (1994); see also Mayes v. Leipziger, 729 F.2d 605, 607 (9th Cir. 1984) (“A judge’s previous

                                   9   adverse ruling alone is not sufficient bias.”); McCoy v. Stronach, 2021 WL 147989, at *1-2 (E.D.

                                  10   Cal. Jan. 15, 2021) (denying plaintiff’s motion for disqualification based on adverse ruling on

                                  11   motion). Plaintiff also argues the undersigned should recuse himself because the Court ignored

                                  12   his request for a hearing after denying his in forma pauperis application. Id. However, while
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   Plaintiff has filed such a request in some of his other cases pending in this District (see, e.g.,

                                  14   Firsov v. Alaska Airlines, Inc., Case No. 25-cv-2841 NC, ECF No. 10; Firsov v. Frontier Airlines,

                                  15   Case No. 25-cv-2898 SVK, ECF No. 10). he did not file a request in this case. Plaintiff further

                                  16   argues the undersigned should recuse for failure to read Plaintiff’s motion for reconsideration.

                                  17   Mot. at 2. However, the Court did read Plaintiff’s motion for reconsideration and in a separate

                                  18   order denies it. Plaintiff additionally asserts that the IFP motion he filed in the public record

                                  19   disclosed his financial information and the Court was obligated to seal it. However, Plaintiff has

                                  20   not filed a motion to seal or demonstrated that the standards for sealing have been met here.

                                  21          Accordingly, the Court DENIES Plaintiff’s motion to disqualify.

                                  22          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  23

                                  24   Dated: May 19, 2025

                                  25

                                  26
                                                                                                      THOMAS S. HIXSON
                                  27                                                                  United States Magistrate Judge

                                                                                             ORDER DENYING PLAINTIFF'S
                                   7              v.                                         MOTION FOR RECONSIDERATION
                                                                                             OF ORDER DENYING APPLICATION
                                   8     JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORPORATION,                        TO PROCEED IN FORMA PAUPERIS
                                   9                    Defendant.                           Re: Dkt. No. 13
                                  10

                                  11          In this civil case, Plaintiff Sergey Firsov moved for permission to proceed “in forma
                                  12   pauperis” under 28 U.S.C. § 1915(a)(1) without prepayment of court filing fees. ECF No. 2. On
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   April 18, 2025, the Court denied Plaintiff’s motion and required him to pay the filing fees by May
                                  14   6, 2025, or risk dismissal of his case. ECF No. 6. After Plaintiff failed to pay the filing fee, the
                                  15   Court ordered him to show cause why this case should not be dismissed for failure to prosecute
                                  16   and failure to comply with court deadlines. ECF No. 11. The Court informed Plaintiff that if he
                                  17   wishes to attempt to proceed with this action, he must either respond to the show cause order or
                                  18   pay the $405.00 filing fee by May 22, 2025. Plaintiff now moves for reconsideration of the order
                                  19   denying his application. ECF No. 13.
                                  20          Under Civil Local Rule 7-9(a), a motion for reconsideration may be granted before entry of
                                  21   judgment adjudicating all of the claims and rights and liabilities of all the parties in a case. Civ.
                                  22   L.R. 7-9(a). A motion for reconsideration may be made on three grounds: (1) a material
                                  23   difference in fact or law exists from that which was presented to the court, which, in the exercise
                                  24   of reasonable diligence, the moving party did not know at the time of the order for which
                                  25   reconsideration is sought; (2) the emergence of new material facts or a change of law; or (3) a
                                  26   manifest failure by the court to consider material facts or dispositive legal arguments. Civ. L.R.
                                  27   7‑9(b). Motions for reconsideration are disfavored and “should not be granted, absent highly
                                  28   unusual circumstances, unless the district court is presented with newly discovered evidence,
                                         Case 3:25-cv-03387-TSH            Document 16         Filed 05/19/25      Page 2 of 2




                                   1   committed clear error, or if there is an intervening change in the controlling law.” McDowell v.

                                   2   Calderon, 197 F.3d 1253, 1255 (9th Cir. 1999) (per curiam) (internal quotation and citation

                                   3   omitted). Furthermore, “[a] motion for reconsideration ‘may not be used to raise arguments or

                                   4   present evidence for the first time when they could reasonably have been raised earlier in the

                                   5   litigation.’” Marlyn Nutraceuticals, Inc. v. Mucos Pharma GmbH & Co., 571 F.3d 873, 880 (9th

                                   6   Cir. 2009) (quoting Kona Enters., Inc. v. Estate of Bishop, 229 F.3d 877, 890 (9th Cir. 2000)).

                                   7          In his motion, Plaintiff states the Santa Clara County Department of Child Support

                                   8   Services has charged his employment account $4,000 per month. Mot. at 1. However, Plaintiff

                                   9   has shown that he is employed and earns approximately $132,000 per year gross salary. ECF No.

                                  10   2. In other cases he has recently filed in this District, see Mot. at 1 (“Plaintiff has more 11 [sic]

                                  11   federal cases”), Plaintiff has also shown that his wife earns additional income and that he recently

                                  12   has paid to fly internationally on multiple flights involving himself, his family, and his dogs. See,
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   e.g., Firsov v. Alaska Airlines, Inc., Case No. 25-cv-2841 NC, ECF No. 15 (denying motion for

                                  14   reconsideration of order denying in forma pauperis application after conducting evidentiary

                                  15   hearing); Firsov v. Frontier Airlines, Case No. 25-cv-2898 SVK, ECF No. 5 (4/3/25 denial of IFP

                                  16   application); Firsov v. Scandanavian Airlines of N. Am., Case No. 25-cv-3691 KAW, ECF No. 6

                                  17   (5/2/25 denial of IFP application); Firsov v. Austrian Airlines, Case No. 25-cv-3504 NC, ECF No.

                                  18   9 (4/28/25 denial of IFP application); Firsov v. Air Canada, Inc., Case No. 25-cv-4058 LJC, ECF

                                  19   No. 4 (in forma pauperis application stating Firsov grosses $10,400 and his wife grosses $1,000

                                  20   per month). Accordingly, the Court finds Plaintiff fails to satisfy any of the grounds for

                                  21   reconsideration under Local Rule 7-9, and his motion is therefore DENIED.

                                  22          In the interest of justice, the Court hereby extends the deadline for Firsov to pay the filing

                                  23   fee to June 5, 2025. ECF 11. If he does not pay the filing fee, the Court will recommend the

                                  24   dismissal of his case without prejudice.

                                  25          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  26   Dated: May 19, 2025

                                  27
                                                                                                      THOMAS S. HIXSON
                                  28                                                                  United States Magistrate Judge
